title: introduce-credential-profiles-and-pausable-stream-facade-ts-sdk
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: unify credential configuration across SDKs and provide a lightweight, pausable streaming facade for better backpressure handling and ergonomic consumption patterns in TypeScript projects; add credential profiles to allow teams to declare reusable auth presets (scopes, TTL hints, rotate window) and enable parity with Py/Go SDK behaviors. What this PR does: 1) introduces a new CredentialProfileRegistry and a small credential template DSL that maps to existing token providers; 2) implements a PausableStreamFacade that exposes pause()/resume() semantics, explicit drain handling, and hintable backpressure callbacks; 3) surfaces retry presets tied to credential profiles so consumers can pick recommended backoff/timeout combinations; 4) updates TypeScript types and examples and adds interop tests against the Python and Go test fixtures to validate parity; 5) bumps package version to 1.28.0 and updates changelog. Compatibility and migration: consumers that previously wired custom token logic can adopt profiles by registering a profile and swapping the simple factory helper; the existing TokenProvider interface is fully backward-compatible. Testing and CI: unit tests for profile parsing, integration tests that spin up the local mock server and validate pause/resume semantics, and e2e smoke tests that exercise retry-presets under injected transient failures. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in linear) - [x] Type definitions and exported API stable - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Docs examples updated - [x] Version bump and changelog entry - [x] Cross-SDK parity tests added Notes: kept the surface intentionally minimal to avoid ergonomic surface area bloat; added opt-in advanced hooks for teams that need fine-grained control. Related: ties into ENG-5214 (credential profiles) and ENG-5230 (stream ergonomics).

review_comments: Evan Liu: Can we collapse the registry API surface to a single `register(name, provider)` call? Prefer minimal public API surface for 90% users.
Priya Nair: Reply: I kept addProfile/getProfile to allow introspection for tooling; collapsing makes some telemetry use-cases awkward. Open to a small helper alias if reviewers prefer.
Maya Alvarez: Tests look good but add a test covering pause()+resume() with multiple parallel consumers to ensure no token thrash.
Priya Nair: Added parallel-consumers test and validated with flaky-run=10 locally; pushed fix to debounce resume notification.
Carlos Fernandez: Type signatures are great; please add a short migration note in README about switching from direct TokenProvider wiring to profiles.
Priya Nair: Added README snippet and example in examples/credential_profiles.md
release_notes: Added credential profiles for reusable auth presets; introduced a pausable streaming facade for ergonomic pause/resume with backpressure hints; tied retry presets to credential profiles; bumped SDK to v1.28.0. See examples/credential_profiles.md for migration guidance.
merge_outcome: Merged to main after approvals from Evan Liu and Maya Alvarez and CI green. No rollback required; version published to npm registry as @redwood-sdk/core@1.28.0.
